events.text: Pelican egg made under Fabergé supervision by workmaster Perkhin

evidence.quote: is a jewelled Easter egg made under the supervision of the Russian jeweller Peter Carl Fabergé in 1898
The egg was created by Faberges workmaster , Mikhail Evlampievich Perkhin
for many years the Pelican Egg was ascribed to 1897

events.text: Egg presented by Nicholas II to Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna for Easter

evidence.quote: presented it to his mother , the Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna on Easter 1898
this Egg was presented to Maria Feodorovna for Easter 1898

events.text: Egg sold by the Antikvariat to Armand Hammer in New York City

evidence.quote: In 1930 , the Imperial Pelican Fabergé egg , with the eight oval miniatures , was one of ten Imperial eggs sold

events.text: Lillian Thomas Pratt purchased the egg from Hammer Galleries (between 1936 and 1938)

evidence.quote: Between 1936 and 1938 it was purchased by Lillian Thomas Pratt

events.text: Egg willed by Mrs. Pratt to Virginia Museum of Fine Arts on her death

evidence.quote: Mrs . Pratt willed the Egg to the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts in Richmond , Virginia , upon her death in 1947

undated_mentions: Armand Hammer showed the egg at department stores across the United States
